Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocol: Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocols are myelosuppressive and require strict hepatic / renal monitoring in infants (often <1 yr old). LVEF threshold 55% (not 50%) in pediatric oncology reflects long-life-expectancy sensitivity to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Larotrectinib / entrectinib much better tolerated than cytotoxic in this age group — the organ-dysfunction flag pushes harder toward TRK-inhibitor monotherapy when fusion-positive (which is >90% of cases). For TRK-inhibitor: dose by BSA / weight per FDA pediatric label; hepatic dose reduction required at bilirubin >3× ULN.
Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DI: Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents + siblings. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is a separate (non- DICER1) etiology that shares the Wilms-spectrum abdominal-tumour surveillance protocol (abdominal US q3-4 months from birth to age 7; AFP q2-3 months from birth to age 4 — focused on hepatoblastoma). Treatment: maximal safe surgical resection (nephron-sparing partial nephrectomy when anatomically feasible; total nephrectomy if not). Histopathology after resection is critical — distinguishes pure cystic nephroma (benign-borderline, surveillance only) from cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma (Wilms-spectrum, requires adjuvant chemo per stage) and from progression to anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney (high-grade malignant, requires multimodal therapy). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: chest imaging (PPB risk), abdominal-pelvic US (ovarian, Sertoli-Leydig risk in girls), thyroid US, and CNS imaging (pineoblastoma, pituitary blastoma risk under age 5).
Pediatric infection screening is broader: Pediatric infection screening is broader than adult — include CMV / herpes given immunosuppression on VAC and likelihood of reactivation in neonates / infants. HBsAg+ infants: confirm vertical transmission, consult pediatric hepatology, entecavir / tenofovir prophylaxis adapted to weight. HIV+ pediatric: ART coordination critical — TRK inhibitors (larotrectinib, entrectinib) are CYP3A4 substrates, avoid CYP3A4 inhibitors. Pneumocystis prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) is standard on cytotoxic arm. Surfaces hold via parallel pre-treatment workup.
Pediatric-inspired adolescent-young-adul: Pediatriskt inspirerade protokoll för ungdomar och unga vuxna dominerar i passform < 40; > 65 dödlighet från induktionstoxicitet är hög. Mini-HCVD + inotuzumab/blinatumomab uppnår bättre tolerabilitet med jämförbar CR-frekvens.

Pexidartinib (PLX3397), a CSF1R/KIT/FLT3 inhibitor, is FDA-approved (August 2019) for adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) associated with severe morbidity or functional limitations not amenable to improvement with surgery. ILLUMINATE phase III trial (Tap et al., Lancet 2019): N=120 (pexidartinib vs placebo, crossover design); primary endpoint ORR at week 25 by RECIST 1.1 and TTP-MRI. ORR: 38% (RECIST) vs 0% placebo (p<0.0001); 56% by TTP-MRI vs 0%. mDOR: not reached at median 23.1 months follow-up. Clinical benefit rate: 56%. Safety: significant hepatotoxicity (cholestatic hepatitis, including one fatal case in open-label extension); ALT/AST elevations in ~51%; FDA REMS program mandatory. EMA approved for same indication (2020). No biomarker companion diagnostic required — all TGCT patients are eligible based on clinical criteria (symptomatic, surgery-resistant). CSF1R IHC or COL6A3-CSF1 fusion testing is not required for treatment initiation.

Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secr: Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor of adrenal medullary origin; extra-adrenal counterparts (paragangliomas) arise from sympathetic / parasympathetic ganglia (head/neck, thoracic, abdominal). They are biologically and clinically a single spectrum (PPGL); this entity is anchored to the adrenal subset for ICD-10 cleanliness but cross-references SDHx-driven extra-adrenal paragangliomas in prevention workstream notes. Hereditary fraction is the highest known among adult cancers (~30–40%). NCCN and Endocrine Society recommend germline panel testing (RET, VHL, SDHB/C/D/AF2, NF1, TMEM127, MAX, FH) for ALL patients with PPGL — not restricted by family history. This makes PPGL a sentinel disease for hereditary cancer surveillance pathways (RET → MEN2 prophylactic thyroidectomy; VHL → multi-organ surveillance; SDHB → lifetime PPGL + RCC surveillance). Classical clinical triad: headache + palpitations + sweating; many patients present with paroxysmal or sustained hypertension. Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical em: Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical embryonal CNS manifestations of DICER1 syndrome — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing regardless of family history. Distinct from pineocytoma (Grade 1, benign) and pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation (PPTID, Grade 2-3). Treatment philosophy parallels other embryonal CNS tumours: maximal safe surgical resection (gross total resection is prognostically dominant); craniospinal irradiation in age-appropriate patients (deferred under age 3 due to neurocognitive toll); adjuvant high-dose chemotherapy regimens (often COG/SIOP protocols with carboplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, etoposide combinations + autologous stem-cell rescue in high-risk cases). Trilateral retinoblastoma (bilateral RB1-carrier with pineal pineoblastoma) historically had near-uniform mortality; modern MRI surveillance from RB1-carrier diagnosis has shifted some cases to earlier detection with improved outcomes.

Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that: Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that binds penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis, producing rapid bactericidal activity against most Gram-negative bacilli including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, most Enterobacterales, many anaerobes, and selected Gram-positive cocci. Tazobactam is an irreversible β-lactamase inhibitor (penicillanic acid sulfone) that binds and inactivates plasmid-mediated and chromosomal class A β-lactamases (TEM, SHV, CTX-M ESBLs partially), restoring piperacillin activity against many β-lactamase-producing organisms. First-line empiric monotherapy for febrile neutropenia (FN) at most centers per IDSA, ECIL-4, and NCCN guidelines because of pseudomonal coverage, anaerobic activity, and good safety profile.

Pituitary blastoma is the strongest sing: Pituitary blastoma is the strongest single-tumour DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any infant should immediately trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents (>95% pituitary blastomas carry pathogenic germline DICER1). Distinct from far-more- common pituitary adenomas (which are not DICER1-driven and are typically adult-onset). Treatment: trans-sphenoidal or trans-cranial resection (technically challenging in infants — pituitary blastomas are bleeding-prone and locally invasive); adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-VP16-cyclophosphamide-based regimens reported in case series); RT generally avoided under age 3 due to severe neurocognitive + endocrine toll. Hypercortisolism management (medical adrenal blockade, sometimes adrenalectomy) is an essential pre-operative bridge. Lifelong endocrine replacement (hydrocortisone, growth hormone, thyroid, gonadal axis) after curative-intent resection. Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for survivors.

Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule in: Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule inhibitor of all three AKT serine/threonine kinase isoforms (AKT1, AKT2, AKT3) within the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway. Suppresses downstream phosphorylation of effector substrates (FOXO, GSK3, TSC2, MDM2, 4EBP1 via mTORC1), reducing proliferation and survival signaling and partially reversing endocrine-therapy resistance in HR+ breast cancer driven by PI3K-pathway alterations. Tumors with activating PIK3CA / AKT1 mutations or PTEN loss (~40-50% of HR+/ HER2- mBC after CDK4/6i) are enriched for response. Pivotal evidence CAPItello-291 (HR+/HER2- mBC after AI ± CDK4/6i): capivasertib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant — overall mPFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo HR 0.60; in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup mPFS 7.3 vs 3.1 mo HR 0.50. FDA approval Nov 2023 (mutation-restricted).
Potent inhibitor of multiple receptor ty: Potent inhibitor of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases: VEGFR-1/2/3, PDGFR-α/β, c-KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R, RET. Antiangiogenic + direct antiproliferative effects. In pNET: anti-VEGF/PDGF pathway disrupts tumour neovasculature; direct TKI effect on pNET cells that overexpress VEGFR. Raymond 2011 NEJM: mPFS 11.4 vs 5.5 mo (HR 0.42) in well- differentiated progressive pNET.

Pre-existing autoimmune disease is prese: Pre-existing autoimmune disease is present in ~10-15% of patients eligible for ICI therapy; historically excluded from pivotal trials. Real-world data (Abdel-Wahab 2018, 3557 pts) shows 55% experienced irAE flare and ~29% required systemic immunosuppression beyond steroids. Risk stratification by SITC 2021: - **Low risk** (generally safe to proceed with monitoring): thyroiditis, vitiligo, stable psoriasis, type 1 diabetes — irAE flare mild, manageable. - **Moderate risk** (proceed with specialist input): RA, IBD (Crohn/UC), sarcoidosis, sicca syndrome, psoriatic arthritis — flare rate ~50%; baseline DMARDs often OK to continue (methotrexate, HCQ but NOT high-dose steroids or anti-TNF at start). - **High risk** (strongest caution; consider alternative if available): active autoimmune hepatitis, myasthenia gravis, inflammatory myopathy, neuromyelitis optica — flare can be life-threatening; benefit-risk discussion mandatory. Pulmonary sarcoidosis specifically: ICI-induced sarcoid-like reactions are well-documented (5-7% of patients on ICI), often mimicking disease progression on imaging. Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and f: Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and for multi-day chemotherapy regimens because of long half-life and demonstrated superiority in delayed-phase CINV control vs ondansetron in head-to-head trials (Saito 2009, Aapro 2014). Triple antiemetic regimen for HEC: NK1 antagonist (aprepitant or fosaprepitant) + palonosetron 0.25 mg IV + dexamethasone 12 mg IV day 1, with dex tapered through delayed phase. Akynzeo (netupitant 300 mg + palonosetron 0.5 mg) fixed-dose oral capsule simplifies triple therapy to two pills (Akynzeo + dex) on day 1. Lowest QT signal in 5-HT3 class — preferred when ondansetron contraindicated due to QT concerns or cardiac comorbidity. Minimal CYP-mediated metabolism makes it the safer 5-HT3 choice in polypharmacy patients (e.g., patients on CYP3A4 inhibitors).

Prevention-persona BWS confirmed-carrier: Förebyggande-persona BWS bekräftad-barriär RedFlag (pædiatrisk cancer predisposition Wave M). Motorvägar till FörebyggandePlan för Wilms tumör + hepatoblastoma övervakning: buken US q3mo från barndomen till ålder 8, AFP månadsvisa till ålder 3-4 då q3mot till ålder 4. STUB väntar två-kliniska-Co-lead tecken per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Sjukdom ankar DIS-WILMS används per Wave-M kort; hepatoklastoma cancer-spektrum noteras i motiveringen parade indikationer.
Prevention-persona Costello syndrome con: Förebyggande-persona Costello syndrom bekräftat-barriär RedFlag (pediatrisk cancer predisposition Wave M). Motorvägar till FörebyggandePlan för embryonal-sarkoma övervakning: buk/pelvic US q3-6mo till 8-10 års ålder, därefter urin cytologi + blåsa US från 10 års ålder. Hjärtövervakning är komorbiditetsdriven och hanteras av parad kardiologi väg, inte denna RF. STUB i avvaktan på två-kliniska-Co-Lead tecken per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Sjukdomsförankring DIS-SOFT-TISSUE-SARCOMA täcker embryonala RMS; neuroblasterm + blåsa TCC cancerspektrum noteras i motiveringen parade indikationer.
Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 a: Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic H. pylori (positive UBT / stool antigen / biopsy histology / stool PCR) AND no confirmed gastric malignancy. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending eradication therapy (per IND-H-PYLORI-PREVENTION-ERADICATION) as the etiological-cancer- prevention pathway. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric cancer causation (IARC Group 1): multiple Cochrane meta-analyses show eradication reduces gastric adenocarcinoma incidence (RR ~0.54-0.66, NNT ~15-50 depending on population baseline incidence). Effect is stronger in high-incidence populations and in younger individuals where atrophic gastritis / intestinal metaplasia has not yet developed. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric MALT lymphoma: eradication is the first-line treatment for early-stage gastric MALT lymphoma, with Wotherspoon regression in ~70-80% of cases (especially t(11;18)- negative). This is treatment-persona territory (existing MALT lymphoma in setting of confirmed H. pylori → treatment Indication, not yet authored) — distinct from prevention persona (chronic H. pylori → prevent MALT/adenocarc...

Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic HCV (HCV-RNA detectable OR HCV-Ab+ with persistent viremia >6 months) AND no confirmed B-cell NHL diagnosis. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending DAA antiviral therapy (per IND-CHRONIC-HCV-PREVENTION-DAA) as the etiological-cancer-prevention pathway. Evidence for HCV → NHL causation (IARC Group 1): multiple cohort studies show 2-3x increased risk of indolent B-cell NHL in chronic HCV carriers; epidemiology especially robust for MZL subtypes. DAA cure (SVR12) has been associated with reduced NHL incidence in post-treatment cohorts (de-Re et al. and others) and with regression of established HCV-associated indolent NHL (the basis of IND-HCV-MZL-1L-ANTIVIRAL for the treatment persona). This is a STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode exemption (sources cited, draft flag set). Engine consumption is DEFERRED to v0.2 implementation wave — the PreventionPlan code path does not yet exist; this RF lands as schema-valid declarative content awaiting that wave.
Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red: Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red-meat ≥500g/week + processed-meat ≥50g/day thresholds per WCRF/AICR + IARC Monograph 114. Severity:major because processed-meat exposure is Group-1 carcinogen with population-attributable fraction ~13% for CRC (WCRF/AICR). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary substitution + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Coexists with existing RF-LIFESTYLE-PROCESSED-MEAT-PREVENTION — both may fire.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heter: Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heterozygous carriers. Distinction from biallelic A-T phenotype is critical: heterozygotes have cancer predisposition only (no neurologic phenotype). Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + pancreatic surveillance for FDR-of- PDAC carriers per CAPS consortium 2022; prostate awareness for males. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BAP1 synd: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för BAP1-syndrom familj historia. STUB väntar på två-Co-Lead sign.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 heterozygous carriers. Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + ovarian symptom-driven workup. NCCN places BARD1 in moderate-elevated breast tier (annual mammography from age 40; consider MRI). Triple-negative subset signal may justify earlier or MRI-inclusive screening in family- history-stratified cohorts. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN confirmed carriers. Multi- organ surveillance: abdominal MRI q2-3y from age 20 for RCC (avoid radiation; many BHD lesions are hybrid oncocytic + slow-growing); chest HRCT baseline + symptom-driven (spontaneous pneumothorax triggers high-resolution imaging); dermatology q1y for skin surveillance. Nephron-sparing surgery (partial nephrectomy) preferred for ≤3cm renal lesions given multifocal/bilateral disease pattern. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BRIP1 het: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för BRIP1 heterozygota bärare. NCCN stöder RRSO vid avslutad fertil eller ålder 45-50; ingen population ovariecancer screening rekommenderas. Bröstövervakning per allmän scheman om inte familjehistoria oberoende höjar risken. STUB i avvaktan på två-Co-Lead avskrivning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinens: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för C. sinensis-driven kolangiocarcinom förebyggande. Brandar på dokumenterad exponeringshistoria med bekräftande testning. Motorvägar till FörebyggandePlan rekommendera praziquantel (om aktiv infektion) + livslång hepato gallvägsövervakning (US + CA 19-9 q12mo från 40 års ålder i kraftigt exponerade kohorter). STUB väntar på Co-Lead granskning. Cancer omfattning: förankrad till DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Östasiatisk endemiskt bälte har 10-50x högre kolangiokarcinom incidens än icke-endemisk västerländska populationer. Geografiskt sammanhang: relevant för östasiatiska diaspora, invandrare, flyktingar, adopter. Samspel med RF-OPISTHORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (Mekongregionen lever-fluke väg, biologiskt liknande mekanism – identisk övervakningsprotokoll).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDH1 / HD: Förebyggande-person RedFlag för CDH1 / HDGC bekräftade transportörer per CONSLC 2020 internationella riktlinje. Prophylactic total gastrectomy (PTG) rekommenderas i åldern 20-30 (intervall 18-40 per individualiserad diskussion); endoskopisk övervakning erkänns underlägsen PTG (diffuse-type signet-ring cell foci dåligt synlig) men erbjuds till PTS-degressiva transportörer. Kvinnliga transportörer: BRCA-liknande bröstövervakning från 30 års ålder. STUB i avvaktan på två-Co-Lead avsignering per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDKN2A-sp: Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDKN2A-specific carriers (gene-specific RF vs the broader FAMMM RF). Pancreatic surveillance per CAPS Consortium 2018/2020: alternating EUS + abdominal MRI/MRCP every 12 months from age 40 OR 10 years before earliest PDAC in family (whichever earlier). Melanoma surveillance: annual full-body skin examination + dermoscopy from age 10-12; mapping photography for multiple atypical moles. Patient should know aggressive sun protection + lifelong CDKN2A-specific cohort. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CHEK2 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for CHEK2 heterozygous carriers. Risk estimates vary substantially by variant: truncating > splice > missense. Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance (annual mammography from age 40 + MRI consideration), modestly tightened CRC screening (colonoscopy from age 40 with q5y interval per NCCN), and prostate awareness from age 40-45 for males with c.1100delC. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CMMRD con: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för CMMRD bekräftad barn-korrigerad kohort. Surveillance per Care for CAMPRD (C4CMMRd) konsortium 2014: helkropps MRI årligen från diagnos; hjärn MRI q6mo från 2 års ålder; kolosokopi q6mos från 6 års ålder, övre GI endoskopi + liten-bowel kapsel årligen 8 år; CBC + serumprotein elektrofores + buken US q6mot. Caskad testning av syskon + föräldra MMR bärare bekräftelse. Immunterapi (anti-PD-1) effektiv i etablerad CAMMD-relaterad cancer (Bouffet 2016, Larkin/CheckMate-serien). STUB i avvaktan på två-Co-Lead avskrivning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite: Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite-Canada syndrome. risk_category set to chronic_condition (not genetic) because etiology is acquired autoimmune-like + non-Mendelian. Surveillance: colonoscopy q1-2y from diagnosis; upper endoscopy q1-2y; small-bowel capsule q2y; treat active disease with immunosuppression (prednisone taper + azathioprine maintenance) + nutritional support (protein replacement, electrolyte correction). Mortality reduced markedly with immuno- suppression treatment. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DES in-ut: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för DES in-utero exponering kohort. Övervakning intensifieras i förhållande till allmän population (årlig bäcken med noggrann vaginal/cervical inspektion, kolposkopi om onormal cytologi, mammografi vid yngre åldersgräns per NCCN-modifierande risk; överväga MRI bröstscreening adjunct given dubbel risk). STUB i avvaktan på två-Co-Lead tecken per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DICER1 co: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för DICER1 bekräftad-barriär kohort. Pediatrisk övervakning per International PPB Registry / IDSDB rekommendationer: - Bröst CT q4-6 mo från födelse till ålder 3, q6-12 mo till ålder 8. - Abdominal US q3-6 mo fr.o.m. födelse till åldern 8. - Sköldkörtel US baslinje efter ålder 8 + q3-5 y. - Pelvic USA i kvinnliga transportörer fr.m menarke. - Hjärn MRI baslinje + symptomdriven. Kirurgi botad för PPb typ I när upptäckt tidigt, avancerad PPBS typ III (fast komponent) mycket aggressiv. Riskreducerande ochorectomy ej godkänt för Sertoli-Leydig förebyggande. STUB avvaktar två-Co-Lead avskrivning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-drive: Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-driven cancer prevention in immunocompromised hosts. Unlike HCV/HBV/H. pylori, there is no curative anti-EBV regimen; the prevention pathway is (a) reduce immunosuppression where feasible, (b) preemptive rituximab in post-transplant patients with rising EBV-DNA (per international PTLD guidelines), (c) periodic EBV-DNA monitoring. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Gating by additional immunocompromise context is deliberate — EBV seroprevalence is >90% in immunocompetent adults globally, so a RF triggered on EBV alone would fire universally and provide no clinical signal.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for FAMMM / C: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för FAMMM / CDKN2A. STUB i avvaktan på två-Co-Lead avskrivning.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on HBsAg+ OR detectable HBV-DNA in patient without HCC. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending nucleos(t)ide analog suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HBV-PREVENTION-ANTIVIRAL) + AFP+US HCC surveillance q6mo per AASLD protocol. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchor target DIS-HCC. HBV-associated DLBCL/NHL is also documented in literature but with weaker effect-size data than the HCV-NHL link; covered via the broader NHL prevention surveillance bullet in the antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-UNIVERSAL-HBV-REACTIVATION-RISK (existing) which is the treatment-time RF for HBV reactivation during anti-CD20 / chemo.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than either mono-infection RF — coinfection carries documented synergistic HCC risk AND DAA-cure-induced HBV reactivation risk that requires combination antiviral. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending concurrent DAA + nucleos(t)ide analog + intensified HCC surveillance (US + AFP q4-6mo, more frequent than the q6mo cadence for either mono-infection). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. NHL prevention (HCV-driven) continues to be a secondary benefit; tracked via prose in the combined-antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HCV-NHL-PREVENTION-OPPORTUNITY and RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence over the two individual RFs (higher priority).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-dri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-driven malignancy prevention. Fires on HHV-8 seropositivity in HIV+, transplant, or other immunocompromised host without confirmed Kaposi sarcoma / MCD / PEL. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending immune restoration (ART for HIV+; transplant-immunosuppression rebalance) + mucocutaneous + oral + GI / lymph-node surveillance. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-KAPOSI. MCD and PEL are HHV-8-driven but not yet authored as distinct Disease entities — covered via the prose surveillance rationale in the indication for now. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (existing) — that is HIV-as-RF; this is HHV-8-positivity-as-RF (the co-factor that turns HIV-related immunocompromise into Kaposi risk specifically).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than mono-infection HBV RF — coinfection carries documented accelerated-fibrosis + elevated HCC risk AND a hard constraint on antiviral selection (tenofovir-based ART mandatory; entecavir monotherapy contraindicated). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending tenofovir-based ART (covers both viruses simultaneously) + AASLD HCC surveillance q6mo. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. HIV-driven AIDS-defining malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma via HHV-8 reactivation, NHL, cervical) are covered separately via RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HHV8-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence (higher priority) and the indication enforces tenofovir-based ART selection.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on positive HIV serology in patient without AIDS-defining or HIV-associated malignancy. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending durable ART suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HIV-PREVENTION-ART) + cancer screening cadence (annual anal cytology in MSM/HIV+; q3-yearly cervical Pap in WLHIV; opportunistic Kaposi/oral hairy leukoplakia visual screening). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the canonical HIV-associated NHL. KS, cervical, anal, Hodgkin, HCC are also HIV-associated; covered via screening recommendations in the ART indication rationale rather than discrete Disease anchors (until DIS-KAPOSI etc. land in v0.2-A authoring backlog).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPRC. STU: Förebyggande personalen RedFlag för HPRC. STUB väntar på två-Co-Lead avskrivning.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on persistent high-risk HPV positivity OR incomplete/absent vaccination in age-eligible individual. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending vaccination (Gardasil-9) and/or risk-group-appropriate screening cadence (cervical: USPSTF Pap+HPV co-test q5y ages 30-65; anal: HRA + cytology q1y in MSM/HIV+/post-transplant). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CERVICAL and DIS-ANAL-SCC. Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and vulvar/vaginal/penile not yet in KB — v0.2-A authoring backlog.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-dr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-driven ATLL prevention. Unlike HCV/HBV/H. pylori, there is no curative regimen — the intervention is surveillance + transmission prevention, not cure. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Geographic context: HTLV-1 endemic regions include Japan (southwest), Caribbean basin, parts of sub-Saharan Africa, parts of South America, Middle East. Ukraine is low-prevalence; this RF is more relevant for diaspora patients or those with travel/origin from endemic regions.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 the: Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 therapeutic-dose lifetime cumulative exposure. Surveillance: CBC q12mo for leukemia signal (sensitivity modest); breast surveillance per general-population USPSTF unless additional risk factors; oral + salivary symptom awareness. Highest-impact preventive intervention is hydration + lemon-juice sialagogue during I-131 administration (reduces salivary gland uptake) — retrospectively non-actionable for prior exposure. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAF: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för MASLD/NAFLD HCC risk. Cirrhotic MASld uppfyller AASLD HTC-övervakning tröskel (US ± AFP q6mo). Non-cirrhot avancerad fibros är en gråzon — närmare hepatologi uppföljning men ännu inte rutinövervakning. Större åtgärdbar spak: viktminskning + hjärtmetabolit hantering. STUB avvaktar två-Co-lead tecken per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confi: Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confirmed-carrier / clinical- diagnostic-criteria-met cohort. Multi-organ surveillance: pediatric ophthalmology q6-12mo to age 8 (optic glioma); whole-body MRI for MPNST surveillance + symptom-driven biopsy of growing/painful/ neurologically-symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas; women: annual mammography from age 30, MRI from age 30-50. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverr: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för O. viverrini-driven kolangiocarcinom förebyggande. Brandar på någon dokumenterad exponeringshistoria med bekräftande test. Motorvägar till FörebyggandePlan rekommenderar praziquantel (om aktiv infektion) + livslång hepato gallvägsövervakning (US + CA 19-9 q12mo från 40 år i kraftigt exponerade kohorter). STUB väntar på co-lead granskning. Cancer omfattning: förankrad till DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Nordöstra Thailand har världens högsta kolangiokarcinom incidens (upp till 90 per 100K) — tillskriven bråkdel i endemiska regioner överstiger 50%. Geografiska sammanhang: relevant för Mekongregionen diaspora, flyktingar, resenärer och adopterade. Kompanjon till RF-CLONORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (östasiatiska lever-fluke väg, biologiskt liknande mekanism).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 het: Förebyggande-person RedFlag för PALB2 heterozygota bärare. PAL B2 närmar sig BRCA2 bröstcancer penetrance och garanterar BRCA-liknande övervakning med årlig bröst MRI + mammografi från 30 års ålder, plus pankreasövervakning (EUS eller MRI växelvis årligen från 50 års ålder eller 10 år innan tidigast PTC i familjen) för FDR-of-PDAC bärare per CAPS konsortium 2022. RRSO diskussion skjuts upp till BRCA tröskeln ges lägre ovariepenetrans. STUB i avvaktan på två-Co-Lead avskrivning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anov: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för PCOS-anovulation endometrierisk. Skillnad från den breda reproduktiva RF för tydligare routing - PCOS - specifik rådgivning (progestin restaurering, metformin, viktminskning) skiljer sig från generisk reproduktiv-historisk rådgivning. Symptomdriven endometrial biopsi vid onormal blödning ≥6 månaders amenorré pre-menopausala eller någon post-mensuella blödning. STUB i avvaktan på två- Co- bly tecken per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RA: Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RAD51D heterozygous carriers. Approaches BRCA-level ovarian penetrance — NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50. Breast surveillance: individualised by family history; consider annual MRI in additional- risk subset. Olaparib PARP inhibitor active in RAD51C/D-mutant established ovarian cancer (PROfound + GEN-ALL trials). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haemat: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för S. hematobium-driven blåsa SCC förebyggande. Brandar på dokumenterad exponering historia med bekräftande testning. Motorvägar till FörebyggandePlan rekommenderar praziquantel (om aktiv infektion) + livstid urinövervakning (urinalys q6-12mo, cytoskopi + cystoskopi för eventuell ny hematuri). STUB väntar Co-Lead översyn. Cancer omfattning: förankrad till DIS-UROTHELIAL. S. hematobium-driven blåscancer är främst SCC histologi (skillnad från urotelial / övergångscellscancer som dominerar västerländska kohorter) - motorn ytor denna skillnad i förebyggande grundprosa. Geografiskt sammanhang: Ukraina är icke-endemiskt; denna RF är relevant för patienter med diaspora / flykting / resa / ursprung historia från söder om Sahara Afrika, Egypten, Sudan, Jemen, delar av Sydamerika.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-defic: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för SDH-brist. STUB väntar på två-Co-Lead avskrivning.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for active to: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för aktiv tobaksanvändning. Högsta effektmodulerbar cancerrisk-faktor intervention. Motorvägar till förebyggandePlan rekommenderar strukturerad stopprådgivning + farmakoterapi + LDCT lung screening om USPSTF-stödberättigande. STUB väntar på två-klinisk-co-lead avregistrering per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracyc: Förebyggande-personen RedFlag för antracyklin kumulativ dos ≥250 mg/m2. Kardioövervakningsfokus (HF/kardiomyopati); t-AML-övervakning överlappar med separat RF-IATROGENIC-TOPO2-TAML-PREVENTION. Eko q1-5y beroende på riskprofil (ASCO/COG-LTFU-kadence). Motorvägar till PreventionPlan som rekommenderar baslinje + serieeko + BNP. STUB i avvaktan på två-klinisk-co-lead avskrivning per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-: Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-amines → urothelial bladder cancer prevention. Fires on documented occupational exposure. DIS-UROTHELIAL anchor preferred but using DIS-HCC as fallback if not in KB on this branch. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic E: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ETS exposure (household / workplace ≥10y). IARC Group 1 + US Surgeon General-confirmed cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum. Distinct from active-smoking RF. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure elimination (cohabitant smoking cessation / workplace smoke-free policy enforcement / personal mitigation) + USPSTF screening eligibility check + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic P: Förebyggande-persona RedFlag för kronisk PPI-exponering ≥10y. Motorvägar till FörebyggandePlan rekommenderar (1) indikationsgranskning + avskrivning där PPI inte längre behövs (mest vanligt scenario), (2) fastande gastrin + kromogranin A i kohort med ihållande syruppression indikation, (3) EGD med kropps-/fundusbiopsier hos dem med förhöjd gastrin eller symtom; övervakning EGD q3-5y om atrologisk gastritis eller ECL hyperplasi dokumenterad. Förankrad till DIS-GASTRIC (gastrisk NET och atrologisk-gastritis-derivat adenokarcinom både mag-kroppssjukdomar); NET-specifika resultat fördes i indikation prosa. STUB väntar på två-kliniska- Co-lead tecken per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic a: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic anti-TNF biologic exposure ≥3y in pediatric / adolescent / young-adult IBD cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) EBV serology baseline in young adults, (2) B-symptom + lymphadenopathy awareness, (3) annual skin examination (synergistic with concomitant thiopurine + UV), (4) periodic shared-decision discussion of combination- therapy step-down where IBD activity allows (anti-TNF monotherapy has favourable cancer signal vs combination with thiopurine), (5) vaccination catch-up (HPV, HBV, influenza, pneumococcal). Severity = minor — absolute attributable risk in anti-TNF monotherapy is small; the meaningful signal is the combination- with-thiopurine HSTCL warning specifically in pediatric / young- adult cohort, addressed via combination-step-down counseling. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS + DIS-HSTCL. STUB pending two-Clinical- Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic i: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic inorganic arsenic exposure via drinking water >10 µg/L (WHO + US EPA MCL). IARC Group 1 carcinogen with established urothelial, lung, and non-melanoma skin cancer etiology. Anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL per task brief; lung + skin surfaced via relevant_diseases. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match. Primary IO resistance is operationally d: Primary IO resistance is operationally distinct from acquired resistance (PD after initial response >6 months). SITC consensus (Kluger 2020) defines primary resistance as PD within 6 months of IO start. Subsequent options vary by tumor: melanoma — BRAF/MEKi if V600E, T-VEC, TIL therapy at trial centers, IL-2; NSCLC — docetaxel ± ramucirumab, ADC if HER2/TROP2; urothelial — enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab combination remains active even after IO-mono PD per EV-302; RCC — cabozantinib monotherapy or lenvatinib + everolimus. IO-rechallenge is generally not standard but may be considered after >6 months treatment-free + non-PD discontinuation reason.

No current cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, or HCC diagnosis. Prodrug hydrolyzed by carboxylesterases: Prodrug hydrolyseras av karboxylesteraser till aktiv metabolit SN-38 (~100-1000× mer potent än föräldern). SN - 38 stabiliserar topoisomerasen-I/DNA klyvbar komplex, vilket ger engångs DNA-brott som blir dödliga dubbel-strandsbrott under S-fasen replikering. SN-38 glucuronideras av UGT1A1 till inaktiv SN - 38G; patienter som är homozygota för UGT 1A1*28 (Gilbert-syntrome variant) eller * 6 har försämrat clearance och allvarlig neutropeni + diarrérisk – CPIC och FDA- etikett rekommenderar båda test före högdosanvändning.
Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B: Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B6 activation to 4-hydroxy- ifosfamide, which decomposes to ifosforamide mustard — the active DNA- alkylating species producing N7-guanine inter-strand crosslinks and apoptosis in proliferating cells. Side-chain oxidation also generates acrolein (urotoxic — drives hemorrhagic cystitis, neutralized by mesna) and chloroacetaldehyde (the principal neurotoxic metabolite responsible for ifosfamide-induced encephalopathy).

Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycyt: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycytidine. Cell cycle phase-specific (S phase) with G1/S blockade. Activity is histology-restricted: highly active in non-squamous NSCLC and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM); minimal-to-no activity in squamous NSCLC due to higher baseline TS expression in squamous histology. Effective suppression (HBV DNA <2,000 IU/mL, ideally undetectable) is the primary virologic response endpoint per AASLD HBV 2024 and EASL HBV 2025. Sustained suppression reduces HCC incidence by ~50-70% in CHB cirrhotics (REVEAL-HBV cohort; Wong 2013 meta-analysis). Primary non-response or viral breakthrough (≥1-log rise on therapy) prompts adherence review, resistance testing, and regimen change (rare with ETV/TAF/TDF — high genetic barrier). ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs antiviral continuation/switch decisions and is the primary HCC-prevention lever in chronic HBV.
Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral: Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral suppression over time during chronic-HBV antiviral therapy (entecavir or tenofovir TDF/TAF — first- line nucleos(t)ide analogues per AASLD 2024 / EASL 2025). Distinct from BIO-HBV-STATUS (serology-based screening / treatment-decision gate). Two clinical contexts: (1) Treatment monitoring in HBeAg+/HBeAg− chronic HBV: baseline HBV DNA + ALT + HBeAg + HBsAg → start NA → recheck q3 months for first year, then q6 months. Goal: HBV DNA undetectable on treatment; ALT normalization; HBeAg seroconversion (HBeAg+ patients) or HBsAg loss (functional cure — rare on NA monotherapy, ~1% per year). Virologic breakthrough (≥1-log rise from nadir) prompts adherence review then switch (entecavir → tenofovir if NA-naïve resistance). (2) Prophylaxis monitoring during B-cell-depleting therapy (rituximab, obinutuzumab) or anti-CD38 (daratumumab, isatuximab) in HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients: entecavir prophylaxis baseline → HBV DNA q3 months during chemotherapy and for 12+ months post-treatment; any detectable HBV DNA = reactivation, hepatology consult. Quantitative HCV RNA monitoring during direct-acting antiviral (DAA) therapy: pretreatment viral load (baseline), end-of-treatment (EOT), and Sustained Virological Response at 12 weeks (SVR12) are the standard treatment-response milestones (AASLD-IDSA 2023; EASL 2023). SVR12 is the evidence-based cure surrogate. Persistent viraemia after week 4 / EOT or detectable viraemia at SVR12 → relapse; switch to a salvage regimen containing sofosbuvir-velpatasvir-voxilaprevir (POLARIS-1). In HCV-associated MZL, lymphoma-response correlates with virologic response (Arcaini 2014; Hermine 2002); HCV eradication itself is first-line MZL therapy for indolent disease per ESMO MZL 2024. ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs DAA regimen selection / continuation decisions and (in HCV-MZL) drives the primary cancer-directed therapy.

AASLD-IDSA / EASL minimum testing protocol: baseline HCV RNA + genotype + cirrhosis staging; on-treatment HCV RNA at week 4 (optional, evaluates adherence/response — undetectable at week 4 = rapid virologic response, RVR; not a stopping rule for modern DAAs); end-of-treatment HCV RNA at completion (week 8 or 12); SVR12 — undetectable HCV RNA 12 weeks after treatment completion = virologic cure (>95% achievable with current DAAs, durable in >99%). SVR12 = primary efficacy endpoint for HCV cure; SVR24 essentially equivalent. Post-SVR HCC surveillance remains REQUIRED in cirrhotic patients (cumulative HCC risk reduced but not eliminated by cure; AASLD recommends ongoing q6-month US ± AFP for cirrhotics regardless of SVR status). R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AM: R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AML (~70-80% of IDH2-mut AML; ~6-8% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved Aug 2017 for R/R-AML-IDH2 monotherapy (phase 1/2: ORR 38%, CR 19%). 1L combination with azacitidine in unfit patients (AG221-AML-005: ORR 71%). Differentiation syndrome (~14%) — same monitoring + dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade; UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic). IDHENTIFY R/R AML phase-3 did not show OS benefit vs conventional care over all comers but enriched in IDH2-mut who had not received prior HMA. Combination with venetoclax + azacitidine under study. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML: R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML (~20-30% of IDH2-mut AML; ~2-3% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved across both R140 and R172 variants. Some series (Stein et al., Blood 2017) suggest R172K carries lower CR rate than R140Q on enasidenib mono, but still substantial activity. Differentiation syndrome (~14%) and hyperbilirubinemia same as R140Q. Glioma IDH2 R172K is a separate clinical entity (vorasidenib INDIGO trial) — this biomarker is AML-scoped; glioma IDH2 captured under BIO-IDH-MUTATION composite. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R175H is the most common TP53 missense h: R175H is the most common TP53 missense hotspot across all human cancers (~5-7% of TP53-mutant tumors per IARC TP53 Database). Structural class mutant — the R175 substitution to histidine disrupts the DNA-binding domain fold (zinc-coordination region). Beyond loss-of-function (LoF), R175H is a canonical example of mutant-p53 GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (GOF): the mutant protein acquires pro-oncogenic activities (chemoresistance via NF-kB, increased migration/invasion, metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation). Clinical implication: R175H+ tumors generally have worse chemo response than TP53-WT or even other TP53-mut tumors. In AML: TP53-mut (any) including R175H → very poor outcomes with intensive chemo, route to alloSCT or venetoclax-azacitidine + clinical trials. In MM: routes to quadruplet per high-risk cytogenetics composite. Emerging GOF-targeting strategies (eprenetapopt/APR-246, arsenic trioxide for structural mutants) are largely investigational; R175H specifically among the reactivatable structural mutants.
R248 is one of the six most-mutated codo: R248 is one of the six most-mutated codons in TP53 (along with R175, G245, R249, R273, R282). DNA-contact class: R248 sits in the L3 loop and makes direct base-specific contact with the DNA minor groove. Substitution to glutamine (R248Q) abolishes sequence-specific DNA binding while preserving overall fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H). R248Q has well-documented gain-of-function (GOF) activities in mouse models — accelerates tumorigenesis and metastasis beyond simple p53-null. Clinical implications mirror other TP53 hotspots: in AML/MDS routes away from intensive chemo toward venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT; in CLL/MCL/MM contraindicates chemoimmuno or routes to high-risk-cytogenetics regimens. Distinction from R248W (different substitution, also a hotspot) — R248Q tends to retain partial folding while R248W more disruptive; both are pathogenic.
R273 is among the top three most-mutated: R273 is among the top three most-mutated TP53 codons (with R175 and R248). DNA-contact class: R273 directly contacts the DNA major groove via its guanidinium side chain. R→H substitution preserves the thermal stability of the protein fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H) but eliminates specific DNA binding. R273H is one of the best-characterized GOF p53 mutants — promotes chemoresistance via NF-κB activation, drives invasion/metastasis through CXCR4 and RhoA pathways, reprograms metabolism (mevalonate pathway upregulation). Clinical implications mirror the TP53-mutant class: AML/MDS — venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; CLL/MCL — contraindicates chemoimmuno; MM — high-risk cytogenetics composite routes to quadruplet. Notably, R273H tumors are particularly resistant to platinum chemotherapy across solid-tumor types per multiple correlative analyses — relevant for ovarian, lung, esophageal cancer treatment selection.
R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codo: R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codon, often grouped with R248 and R273 as the canonical hotspot ring. Hybrid structural/contact mutant: R282 stabilizes the L1/S3 loop region adjacent to the DNA-binding surface, and R→W partially destabilizes the fold while altering contact geometry. Functional studies show R282W retains partial transactivation activity on a subset of canonical p53 targets (CDKN1A/p21, BBC3/PUMA at reduced levels) — termed "partial LoF" — while still gaining oncogenic activities. Clinically R282W behaves similarly to other hotspots: in AML/MDS poor chemo response → routes to venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; in CLL/MCL/MM high-risk regimen routing. Distinction from full LoF mutants (truncating, splice-site) may matter for emerging mutant-p53 reactivator drugs (eprenetapopt) where residual fold is required — R282W generally considered reactivatable in early-phase trials.

RADIANT-3 (Yao NEJM 2011): everolimus 10: RADIANT-3 (Yao NEJM 2011): everolimus 10 mg/day vs placebo in progressive well-differentiated pNET (n=410). mPFS 11.0 vs 4.6 mo (HR 0.35, p<0.001). No significant OS benefit demonstrated (confounded by >70% crossover post- progression). SSA prior / concurrent use allowed. Stomatitis prophylaxis (dexamethasone mouthwash, SWISH trial) reduces G2+ stomatitis dramatically. Sunitinib 37.5 mg/day is the alternative (Raymond NEJM 2011 — similar mPFS 11.4 vs 5.5 mo, HR 0.42); no head-to-head comparison; choice based on comorbidities (cardiac/renal → prefer everolimus; diabetes/steroids → consider sunitinib). RAI-refractory PTC TKI therapy is multi-: RAI-refractory PTC TKI therapy is multi-year (median PFS 18 mo on lenvatinib SELECT; >25 mo on selpercatinib LIBRETTO) — chronic exposure raises HBV reactivation risk. HIV+: lenvatinib / sorafenib / selpercatinib / dabrafenib / trametinib are all CYP3A4 substrates — coordinate ART to avoid CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir-boosted PIs). Active TB: rifampin (CYP3A4 inducer) lowers TKI exposure significantly — prefer rifabutin if anti-TB needed concurrently.

RB1 alterations (deletion, mutation) occur in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and are enriched in the basal/squamous-differentiated molecular subtype (~50%). RB1 loss is associated with resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (which require pRb to exert G1 arrest). Therapeutic implications in bladder cancer: (1) RB1 loss may associate with sensitivity to immunotherapy (higher genomic instability) — inconsistent evidence; (2) Basal/squamous subtype (often RB1-low) responds better to neoadjuvant chemotherapy than luminal subtypes; (3) No approved targeted therapy exploits RB1 deficiency in bladder cancer as of 2026. ESCAT IIIB: RB1 is a prognostic and potential therapeutic vulnerability marker in urothelial cancer; no approved targeted agent.

RB1 biallelic loss, together with TP53 loss, is the molecular hallmark of SCLC (~95% of cases have both). RB1 loss is not used to select therapy in SCLC (all SCLC patients receive the same backbone: EP/EC ± atezolizumab/durvalumab); rather, it is a diagnostic characteristic and potential therapeutic vulnerability. RB1 loss renders cells dependent on alternative cell cycle regulators (CDK4/6-independent E2F activation) — this is why CDK4/6 inhibitors have no activity in SCLC (pRb loss negates CDK4/6 inhibition). Investigational targeting of RB1-deficient SCLC: aurora kinase A inhibitors (alisertib — phase II, limited activity); EZH2 inhibitors (tazemetostat — RB1-null tumors may have heightened EZH2 dependence); LSD1 inhibitors; ATR/CHK1 inhibitors (replication stress in RB1-null context). ESCAT IIIB: RB1 loss is diagnostically informative and a conceptual therapeutic target, but no FDA-approved targeted therapy exploiting RB1 deficiency as of 2026.

RB1 germline pathogenic variants cause heritable retinoblastoma (~40% of retinoblastoma cases) — bilateral / multifocal disease in 80% of carriers, median age at diagnosis ~12 months. Carriers face lifetime ~50% risk of secondary primary cancers (osteosarcoma, soft-tissue sarcoma, melanoma, lung, bladder); cumulative risk markedly elevated after external-beam radiation therapy (EBRT) — modern protocols avoid EBRT to mitigate. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per COG / Children's Oncology Group + International Retinoblastoma Consortium): pediatric ophthalmology with EUA (examination under anesthesia) starting in newborn period — every 2-4 weeks until age 1, then progressive lengthening to monthly → q3mo → q6mo through age 7, annual through adolescence. Lifelong secondary-cancer surveillance: annual skin exam, attentiveness to bone pain (osteosarcoma in adolescence/young adulthood), avoidance of unnecessary diagnostic ionizing radiation. ESCAT IIA.

Radiotherapy contraindicated or declined for early-stage NLPBL (nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma, WHO 5th ed). Major clinical scenarios: (1) Young patient with breast or thyroid field overlap — cumulative RT dose risk of secondary malignancy and cardiac toxicity unacceptable; (2) Prior RT to the involved or adjacent region — reirradiation risks exceed benefit; (3) Patient refuses RT after informed discussion. In all scenarios rituximab monotherapy (4–8 × R weekly) achieves ~94% ORR with ≥70% CR in early-stage NLPBL (Advani 2014, IELSG-37 data) and is the accepted standard alternative. RT remains the default for eligible patients where field is safe and patient consents (stage IA-IIA, ≤2 cm).

Recombinant non-infectious bivalent HPV: Recombinant non-infectious bivalent HPV vaccine. Each dose contains virus-like particles (VLPs) assembled from the L1 major capsid protein of two HPV types — 16 and 18 — produced in a baculovirus expression system in Trichoplusia ni insect cells (Hi-5) and adjuvanted with AS04 (3-O-desacyl-4'-monophosphoryl lipid A on aluminium hydroxide), a TLR4 agonist designed to enhance and prolong the antibody response. L1 VLPs contain no viral DNA — cannot cause HPV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer neutralizing IgG against HPV 16 and 18; cross- neutralization against types 31, 33, 45, 58 is documented (modest efficacy, lower than direct protection). Recombinant non-infectious nine-valent H: Rekombinant icke-infektiärt nio-valent HPV-vaccin. L1 VLP är immunogena men innehåller inget virus DNA – kan inte orsaka HPV infektion. Vaccination framkallar hög-liters neutraliserande IgG som förhindrar incidenter av de täckta HPV - typerna. Cancer-prevention väg: förhindrar ihållande infektion med HPV-typerna som ansvarar för ~90% av livmoderhalscancer, ~90 % av analcancer, #70% av vaginal/vulvar cancer, ~60% av penilcancer, och en växande bråkdel av orofaryngaryngeal cancer.
Recombinant non-infectious vaccine conta: Recombinant non-infectious vaccine containing hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) produced in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Engerix-B, Recombivax HB) or in mammalian cells (PreHevbrio — tri-antigen S/preS1/ preS2). HBsAg contains no viral DNA — cannot cause HBV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer anti-HBs neutralizing IgG that prevents incident HBV infection on exposure. KB scope choice: ships as biomarker + RF (informational) only — no new IND, no algorithm step. Tx-modifying signal deferred to a future taxane-mCRPC IND chunk that branches on AR-amp / AR-V7 / LBD-mutation status.

Regular consumption of maté (Ilex paraguariensis infusion) prepared and drunk at very high temperatures (≥65°C / ≥149°F) — characteristic of traditional gourd-and-bombilla preparation in southern South America (Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, southern Chile) and diaspora communities. IARC Monograph 116 (2016) classified drinking very hot beverages above 65°C as Group 2A (probably carcinogenic) — limited evidence in humans (consistent associations with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in maté-drinking, hot-tea, and hot-coffee cohorts, with residual confounding from tobacco / alcohol co-exposure not fully excluded), sufficient evidence in experimental animals (thermal injury → chronic inflammation → field carcinogenesis in rodent esophagus models). Important: at temperatures <60°C, no association is observed; maté per se (the herb / its phytochemicals) is NOT classified as carcino...
Regular consumption of very hot beverage: Regular consumption of very hot beverages (≥65°C / 149°F) per IARC Monograph 116 (2016) — applies primarily to teas (especially traditional preparation styles in regions of Iran, Turkey, China, parts of South America with maté), but also coffee/water consumed at scalding temperatures. IARC Group 2A (probably carcinogenic) classification — associated with esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma (ESCC), particularly in regions with high background ESCC incidence. Mechanism: thermal injury to esophageal epithelium → chronic inflammation → field carcinogenesis. Note: at typical Western coffee/tea temperatures (<60°C), no association observed; coffee + tea per se are not carcinogenic. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g: Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g/day per WCRF/IARC threshold. IARC Monograph 114 (2015) classified processed meat as Group 1 carcinogen for colorectal cancer (sufficient evidence). Each 50 g/day of processed meat increases CRC risk by ~18% (meta-analyzed RR ~1.18; WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating). Processed meat = sausages, ham, bacon, salami, cured/smoked/salted/preserved meat. Red meat (Group 2A per IARC, probable carcinogen) is a separate but overlapping concern — threshold ≥500 g/week for red meat. Mechanisms: N-nitroso compounds, heterocyclic amines, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, heme iron. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Relapsed/refractory DLBCL with confirmed CD20 expression on malignant B-cells, post ≥2 prior systemic therapies including one anti-CD20 antibody-containing regimen (R-CHOP), CAR-T-ineligible or post-CAR-T failure — candidate for epcoritamab (CD20xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager; subcutaneous step-up administration). Pivotal data EPCORE NHL-1 phase 1/2 (Thieblemont 2023 J Clin Oncol): ORR 63%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.4 mo, mDOR 12 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T for non-eligible / bridging / post-failure setting. Distinct from glofitamab (different schedule: fixed 12 cycles vs continuous; IV vs SC). CD20-loss escape post-prior-anti-CD20 is a documented mechanism — re-biopsy advisable for late-relapse cohorts.

Relapsed/refractory DLBCL with confirmed CD20 expression on malignant B-cells, post ≥2 prior systemic therapies including one anti-CD20 antibody-containing regimen (R-CHOP), CAR-T-ineligible or post-CAR-T failure — candidate for glofitamab (CD20xCD3 2:1 bispecific T-cell engager; intravenous; fixed 12-cycle duration). Pivotal data NP30179 phase 1/2 (Dickinson 2022 NEJM): ORR 52%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.9 mo, mDOR 18.4 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL after fixed treatment course. Differentiator vs epcoritamab: fixed-duration (12 cycles ≈ 8.3 mo) vs continuous; IV vs SC; obinutuzumab pre-treatment 7 days before C1D1 reduces CRS. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T. Often considered after epcoritamab failure in BiTE-sequencing strategies, though direct comparative data are lacking.

Mechanism: cumulative ovulatory cycles + unopposed estrogen exposure + delayed terminal differentiation of breast ductal epithelium. Revumenib (SNDX-5613), an oral menin inhibitor, is FDA-approved (Nov 2024) for relapsed/refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia (AML and ALL). AUGMENT-101 (Issa et al. NEJM 2023; Erba et al. ASH 2023 update): KMT2A-rearranged R/R AML/ALL — ORR 23% (CR + CRh + CRi), complete remission with full recovery 18%; mOS 8.0 mo. FDA accelerated approval based on remission rate as surrogate endpoint. KMT2A rearrangement is present in ~10% of adult AML (more common in secondary/therapy-related AML and infant leukemia). Menin is an essential co-factor of KMT2A-fusion oncoproteins — revumenib disrupts menin-MLL interaction, restoring differentiation block. Combination strategies under evaluation: revumenib + venetoclax + azacitidine (phase II ongoing). ELN 2022 risk: KMT2A-rearranged AML classified as intermediate risk (specific partner-dependent — MLLT3 intermediate; others may be adverse).

Revumenib (menin inhibitor) FDA-approved (Nov 2024) for relapsed/refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia including B-ALL. AUGMENT-101 combined KMT2A-rearranged cohort (AML + ALL): ORR 23%, CR/CRh 18%. KMT2A rearrangement defines a high-risk B-ALL subset: in infants KMT2A-AFF1 is present in ~80% of infant B-ALL (EFS <30% with standard chemotherapy); in adults KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL is adverse-risk (NCCN/ELN). Revumenib represents a first targeted option for this historically chemotherapy-refractory population. Blinatumomab (CD19 BiTE, FDA-approved for R/R B-ALL) and inotuzumab ozogamicin are also active in KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL regardless of KMT2A status, but revumenib is the first mutation-specific approved agent. AlloHCT in CR remains the standard consolidation for eligible adults.

However, the JAK/STAT pathway is aberrantly activated in MF/SS (~30–50% have JAK3 mutations or JAK1/STAT3/STAT5 alterations), making JAK inhibitors an active investigational area. Phase II evidence: ruxolitinib (oral) ORR ~29% in relapsed/refractory MF (RUXO-MF pilot data); itacitinib (JAK1 inhibitor) and cerdulatinib (JAK/SYK inhibitor) in phase II trials for CTCL. The CTCL-specific approvals are for non-JAK-targeted agents: romidepsin (HDAC inhibitor; FDA 2009 CTCL), brentuximab vedotin (CD30+; FDA 2017), mogamulizumab (CCR4; FDA 2018), vorinostat (FDA 2006). JAK3-mutant CTCL: JAK3 mutation identifies a subset with stronger a priori rationale for JAK inhibitor use; ESCAT IIA reflects absence of dedicated FDA approval in CTCL despite biological rationale and early phase data.

SMARCB1 (INI1/hSNF5/BAF47) is a core sub: SMARCB1 (INI1/hSNF5/BAF47) is a core subunit of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex. Biallelic inactivation removes SWI/SNF antagonism of EZH2 (PRC2 complex), leading to H3K27me3 accumulation and epigenetic silencing of tumor suppressor genes. This makes SMARCB1-deficient tumors selectively sensitive to EZH2 inhibition. SMARCB1 loss defines three main tumor types: (1) Epithelioid sarcoma — tazemetostat FDA-approved (2020; EZH-202 trial). (2) Malignant rhabdoid tumor (MRT, AT/RT in CNS) — extremely aggressive; no approved targeted therapy; investigational EZH2 inhibitors. (3) SMARCB1-deficient chordoma, sinonasal carcinoma — rare. IHC for INI1 (nuclear loss) is the companion diagnostic for tazemetostat in epithelioid sarcoma and is simpler than molecular testing. Note: retained INI1 expression does NOT exclude epithelioid sarcoma — ~10% of cases have normal INI1 by IHC despite molecular loss (technical or heterogeneous loss).

STUB — Wave A+B germline expansion. Linked Indication: none (no Bloom- specific Indication exists yet). Two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff queued. SUFU germline (BMA-SUFU-GERMLINE- MEDULLOBLASTOMA) is the alternate NBCCS-like locus.

STUB — Wave A+B germline expansion. Linked Indication: none (no WT1- specific Indication exists yet). Two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff queued. Other 11p13 contiguous-gene deletion phenotypes (e.g. simultaneous involvement of PAX6) explain aniridia and warrant ophthalmology follow-up.

SUFU germline pathogenic variants cause a Gorlin-syndrome–like predisposition with much higher medulloblastoma risk than PTCH1 (~30% lifetime vs ~5% in PTCH1), and lower BCC burden. SUFU-driven medulloblastomas cluster in the SHH-activated molecular subgroup (infant/young-child onset, desmoplastic / MBEN histology in many cases). Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per Foulkes et al. 2017 / AACR Pediatric Predisposition Working Group): brain MRI q4mo from diagnosis through age 3, q6mo from age 3-5, annually to age 8 — denser-than-PTCH1 cadence reflects higher MB risk. Dermatology surveillance for BCC q6-12mo from puberty. Avoid craniospinal external-beam radiation when alternatives exist (second-malignancy risk in carriers). Hedgehog-pathway inhibitors (vismodegib, sonidegib) have limited activity in SUFU-mutant SHH-MB — downstream-of-SMO position renders SMO inhibitors ineffective; this is a critical distinction from PTCH1-driven disease. ESCAT IIA.

USPSTF 2018: Grade C for men 55-69 (individualized shared-decision-making about benefits + harms); Grade D for men ≥70 (recommend AGAINST routine screening). NCCN 2025 (Early Detection): baseline PSA + DRE discussion at age 45 for African American men or BRCA2 carriers (high-risk groups), age 50 for average risk; if PSA <1 ng/mL, repeat every 2-4 years; if PSA 1-3 ng/mL, repeat every 1-2 years; if PSA >3 ng/mL, evaluate further (repeat PSA, mpMRI, biomarker reflex such as 4Kscore/PHI, possible biopsy). Higher screening intensity for confirmed BRCA2 germline carriers (IMPACT study — PSA q1y starting age 40; biopsy threshold ≥3 ng/mL). PSA can be falsely elevated in BPH, prostatitis, urinary retention, recent instrumentation. Free PSA ratio, PSA density, and reflex biomarkers (PHI, 4Kscore, SelectMDx) reduce unnecessary biopsy. Limitations: overdiagnosis/overtreatment of indolent cancers (well-characterized harm — driver of USPSTF Grade C). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

Selective small-molecule inhibitor of hy: Selektiv liten-molecule hämmare av hypoxia-india-fördubbbar faktor 2α (HIF-2α). Selective, high-affinity D2-dopamine rec: Selective, high-affinity D2-dopamine receptor agonist with a long elimination half-life (~65 hours) permitting once- or twice-weekly oral dosing. Serum AFP is used in combination with ultrasound every 6 months for HCC surveillance in cirrhotic patients of any aetiology (Child-Pugh A/B7, candidates for treatment) and in non-cirrhotic chronic HBV with elevated HCC risk per AASLD HCC 2023. US-alone sensitivity is suboptimal (~63%); US + AFP raises sensitivity for early-stage HCC to ~70-80% with acceptable specificity (~85-90%). AFP threshold typically >20 ng/mL (some guidelines >7 ng/mL with risk-stratified cutoffs). Rising AFP trajectory is more informative than single value. AFP elevation also occurs in chronic hepatitis flares, regenerative nodules, germ-cell tumours, and gestation — interpret in context. Diagnostic workup of rising AFP: multiphasic CT or MRI per LI-RADS criteria. AFP-L3 fraction and DCP (PIVKA-II) are adjunct markers in some practices. ESCAT IIIA — AFP directs HCC diagnostic workup / surveillance cadence.

Serum calcitonin is a highly specific biomarker for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) — produced by parafollicular C-cells. In MEN2 RET germline carriers, calcitonin trends inform timing of prophylactic thyroidectomy (RET codon-stratified per ATA Thyroid 2015 + Endocrine Society MEN 2023): - MEN2B (M918T): prophylactic thyroidectomy <1 year, before calcitonin rise becomes detectable - MEN2A high-risk codons (634, 883): thyroidectomy by age 5 - MEN2A moderate-risk codons (609, 611, 618, 620, 630, 631): may delay until calcitonin becomes detectable on stimulation testing Basal + stimulated (pentagastrin / calcium-stimulated where available) calcitonin tracks residual disease post-thyroidectomy. CEA is a complementary marker. Doubling time of calcitonin post-resection is a strong prognostic indicator (<6 mo = aggressive). ESCAT IIIA — calcitonin directs prophylactic surgery timing and post-operative monitoring.

Shimoyama smoldering or chronic-favourable subtype of ATLL. Smoldering: ≥5% circulating abnormal lymphocytes, no organ involvement (skin/lung lesion permitted), LDH normal, BUN normal, albumin normal, no hypercalcemia, no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. Chronic-favourable: similar to smoldering but lymphadenopathy/organomegaly permitted, LDH ≤2× ULN, BUN ≤ULN, albumin ≥ULN, Ca normal, no CNS/bone/GI/effusion. AZT+IFN-α (anti-HTLV-1 mechanism) yields 5-yr OS ~46% vs ~20% for chemotherapy in these subtypes (Bazarbachi 2010 meta-analysis, JNCI). Aggressive subtypes (acute/lymphoma/chronic-unfavourable) do NOT respond to AZT+IFN — route those to CHOEP+mogamulizumab via RF-ATLL-HIGH-RISK-BIOLOGY.

Sirolimus (rapamycin), an mTORC1 inhibitor, is FDA-approved (May 2015) and EMA-approved (2017) for treatment of LAM in adults. MILES phase III RCT (McCormack et al., NEJM 2011): N=89 (46 sirolimus, 43 placebo); 12-month treatment + 12-month observation. Primary endpoint: FEV1 change from baseline to 12 months (mL/month rate). FEV1 slope: +1 mL/month (sirolimus) vs -12 mL/month (placebo); difference 11 mL/month (p<0.001). Secondary: FVC improvement, VEGF-D reduction, 6-min walk improvement, QoL. After 12-month observation: benefits partially lost (FEV1 decline resumes), suggesting need for continuous therapy. mTOR inhibition does not eliminate LAM cells but controls their mTORC1-driven proliferation. Everolimus is used for TSC-associated LAM and for renal angiomyolipoma (EXIST-2). VEGF-D ≥800 pg/mL is a diagnostic biomarker (non-invasive diagnosis of LAM possible in right clinical context without biopsy).

Small-molecule allosteric inhibitor of m: Small-molecule allosteric inhibitor of mutant IDH2 enzyme (R140Q, R172K hotspots). Mutant IDH2 catalyzes neomorphic conversion of α-ketoglutarate to 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG), an oncometabolite that drives DNA + histone hypermethylation and blocks myeloid differentiation. Enasidenib reduces 2-HG, restoring TET2-dependent demethylation and inducing terminal differentiation of leukemic blasts. FDA-approved Aug 2017 on the basis of phase 1/2 single-arm data in R/R AML (AG221-AML-001).

Avbrytande menin -MLL förarsätter det leukemogena transcriptionsprogrammet, inducerar differentiering och apoptos av leukemiska master. FDA-godkänd Nov 2024 på grundval av AUGMENT-101 fas 1/2 prövning.

Sokal score (Sokal 1984) uses age, splee: Sokal score (Sokal 1984) uses age, spleen size, platelet count, blast %. High-risk (Sokal >1.2) marks ~20-25% of CML-CP at diagnosis with worse 10-yr OS and PFS on imatinib vs intermediate/low. ENESTnd (Saglio 2010) and DASISION (Kantarjian 2010) show 2nd-gen TKIs achieve faster + deeper molecular responses than imatinib in high-Sokal subgroups. ELN 2020 prefers ELTS (RF-CML-HIGH-RISK-ELTS, existing) but Sokal remains the more widely-used bedside score. Companion to RF-HASFORD-HIGH; both can fire together. Conflict- resolution: this RF intensifies toward 2nd-gen TKI; cardiotoxicity flags (RF-CML-COMORBIDITY-COMPLEX) may de-escalate back to imatinib.

Sokal poäng (Sokal 1984) använder ålder, mjältestorlek, trombocytantal, explosionsprocent. Hög risk (Sokaal >1.2) märken ~20-25% av CML-CP vid diagnos med sämre 10-årigt OS och PFS på imatinib vs mellanliggande / låg. ENESTnd (Saglio 2010) och DASSION...

Square-planar platinum(II) coordination: Fjärde planar platina(II) samordningskomplex. Efter cellulär upptag och aquation (Cl förflyttas med vatten i låg-klorid intracellulär miljö), bildar den aktiverade arten intra- och inter-strand DNA korslänkar, främst 1,2-d(GpG) och 1,2-D(ApG). Dessa adducts snedvrider DNA helix, blockerar replikation och transkription, och utlöser apoptos när den inte repareras. Motståndsmekanismerna inkluderar förbättrad nukleotidexcisionsreparation, glutathion avgiftning och minskad cellupptag (CTR1-transportör). Staging at diagnosis + response assessme: Iscensätter diagnos + respons bedömning efter antiviral eller kemoimmuno terapi. Detekterar transformation hotspots.
Standalone authoring of the cycle-1 step: Fristående författare av cykeln-1 steg-upp sub-schema för epcoritamab subkutan dosering. Steg-upp sekvens - 0,16 mg → 0,8 mg → 48 mg - med profylaktiskt prednisolon 100 mg × 4 dagar runt varje dos suppressar alla grader CRS till ~50% (framför allt grad 1-2; G ≥3 ~3%) per EPCORE NHL-1. Sub-regimen enhet som har uppgett separat för att möjliggöra återanvändning över DLBCL / FL / framtida indikationer och för att tillhandahålla en enda enhet för att rengörare till ytan cykel-1 sjukhus-övervakning + kortikosteroid profylax mönster. Bibliografiska rekord SRC-EPCORE-NHL-1-THIEBLEMONT-2023 är tillgängliga, klinisk fordring koppling kräver dubbla kliniska tecken.
Standalone authoring of the obinutuzumab: Fristående auktorisation av den engångsdosen av obinutuzumab som används för att förnedsätta cirkulerande CD20+B-celler 7 dagar före glofitamatcykel 1 dag 1. Mekanistiskt minskar risken för CRS genom att minska det bispecifika T-cellengagersubstratet vid första exponeringen; i NP30179 hölls den kombinerade förbehandlingen med obinutauzumabi + glofitamab steg-upp + kortikosteroid premedicineringsstrategi G ≥3 CRS till ~4%. Standard 12-week varenicline course is t: Standard 12-week varenicline course is the most effective single-agent tobacco-cessation pharmacotherapy (USPSTF + AHCPR). Set quit date day 8 of treatment (~end of titration). Extension to 24 weeks improves long-term abstinence in patients abstinent at 12 weeks. Counsel patients on neuropsychiatric monitoring (EAGLES 2016 reassured but residual caution).
Standard 1L cytoreduction for high-risk: Standard 1L cytoreduktion för högrisktrombos (ålder > 60 eller tidigare trombos) och högrisk-ET (sama kriterier). Standard 1L for AML unfit for intensive: Standard 1L for AML unfit for intensive 7+3 (VIALE-A: median OS 14.7 vs 9.6 mo for aza alone). Standard 1L for MDS-HR (and bridging to: Standard 1L for MDS-HR (and bridging to alloHCT in eligible patients). Azacitidine and decitabine functionally equivalent; choice often local. Standard 1L for R/M HNSCC with CPS ≥1 (t: Standard 1L for R/M HNSCC with CPS ≥1 (the majority of HNSCC). Standard 1L for fit transplant-eligible: Standard 1L för passform transplantationsberättigad MCL (ålder < 65, ECOG 0-1). Nordiskt protokoll eller LYMA-stil. Standard 1L for fit-for-intensive AML. A: Standard 1L för fit-for-intensiv AML. Lägg till midostaurin om FLT3-ITD/TKD+ (RATIFY: förbättrat 4-y OS 51% vs 44%). Standard 1L for low/intermediate-risk AP: Standard 1L for low/intermediate-risk APL (Sanz WBC ≤10). Standard 1L for the imatinib-sensitive G: Standard 1L for the imatinib-sensitive GIST genotypes (~85% of all GIST). Reuses cross-line REG-IMATINIB-GIST-1L which encodes the KIT exon 9 dose-escalation rule.
Standard 1L for the ~50-100% of advanced: Standard 1L for the ~50-100% of advanced MTC that is RET-mutant (sporadic ~50% RET M918T; hereditary MEN2 ~100%). Reuses cross-disease DRUG-SELPERCATINIB.
Standard 1L induction regimen for transp: Standard 1L induction regimen for transplant-eligible MM (4 cycles before harvest, then ASCT, then 2 cycles consolidation, then lenalidomide maintenance). Standard 1L regimen for newly-diagnosed: Standard 1L regimen for newly-diagnosed DLBCL NOS for the past 20+ years. ~60% cure rate overall, ~80% for low-IPI / ~55% for high-IPI. Interim PET-CT after cycles 2-4 helpful for response assessment but doesn't routinely change therapy unless PD seen.
Standard 1L symptom-directed therapy for: Standard 1L symptom-directed therapy for symptomatic PMF (and post-PV/ET MF). COMFORT-I/II: ≥35% spleen-volume reduction in ~42% vs 0.7% placebo; symptom improvement; pooled OS benefit suggested. Does NOT eliminate clone or alter natural history of fibrosis. Standard 2L for SMZL/NMZL after rituxima: Standard 2L för SMZL/NMZl efter fel på behandling med rituximab som monoterapi. ORR ~85-90%; median PFS ~3-4 år. PJP-profylax ≥6 mo efter anti-CD20; HBV reaktiveringsövervakning obligatorisk.
Standard 2L mCRC after FOLFOX progressio: Standard 2L mCRC after FOLFOX progression. Adding bevacizumab (TML / ML18147 trial) improves PFS (5.7 vs 4.1 mo) + OS (11.2 vs 9.8 mo, HR 0.81) over FOLFIRI alone. Anti-EGFR (cetuximab or panitumumab) alternative add-on for RAS-WT left-sided patients in 2L if not used in 1L (or if patient progressed on bevacizumab). UGT1A1 testing recommended before high-dose irinotecan use. Cholinergic syndrome vs delayed diarrhea — distinct pathophysiology + management.
Standard 2L+ for R/R FLT3-mutated AML pe: Standard 2L+ för R/R FLT3-muterad AML per ADMIRAL. Bro till alloHCT för passa kandidater uppnå CR/CRh — Gilteritinib ensam är inte botande. Fortsätt Gilteritainib post-HCt som underhåll (omärkt, stöds av framväxande data MORPHO test). STUB — avvaktande Co-Lead avskrivning.
Standard 2L+ for R/R IDH2-mutated AML pe: Standard 2L+ for R/R IDH2-mutated AML per AG221-AML-001 (FDA approval Aug 2017). Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — enasidenib monotherapy is not curative; durable responses in trial were largely consolidated by alloHCT. Differentiation syndrome (~14%) is the signature AE — same dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade) is biochemical UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic. Bibliographic record SRC-IDHENTIFY is available; SRC-AG221-AML-001 remains a source gap. STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.
Standard 2L+ for R/R KMT2A-rearranged AM: Standard 2L+ for R/R KMT2A-rearranged AML per AUGMENT-101 (FDA approval Nov 2024). Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — revumenib monotherapy is not curative; durable responses in trial were largely consolidated by alloHCT. Differentiation syndrome (~16%) is the signature AE — same dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib / enasidenib. QTc prolongation requires baseline + serial ECG. Bibliographic record SRC-AUGMENT-101 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.

Standard H2 component of chemotherapy pr: Standard H2 component of chemotherapy premedication, paired with H1 antihistamine (diphenhydramine) and corticosteroid (dexamethasone). Particularly important before paclitaxel (Cremophor vehicle hyper- sensitivity), rituximab, daratumumab, and other monoclonal antibodies with significant infusion reaction rates. Combined H1 + H2 blockade is empirically superior to H1 alone for prevention of mild-to-moderate hypersensitivity reactions (Lieberman-Goodyear, 2010). NEVER a substitute for epinephrine in true anaphylaxis — H1 + H2 + steroid treats pruritus, urticaria, mild bronchospasm, but does not reverse hypotension or upper airway edema. Famotidine preferred over cimetidine in oncology because of clean DDI profile (cimetidine inhibits multiple CYPs causing exposure increases of warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin, TKIs, vincristine — major hazard); ranitidine withdrawn worldwide 2019-2020 for NDMA contamination. CRITICAL: H2 antagonists raise gastric pH → reduce absorption of pH-dependent oral oncology agents (dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, dabigatran, atazanavir) — separate by 2-10 h or substitute / time TKI dose. Standard R-CHOP component. Premedication: Standard R-CHOP component. Premedication: 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone. Mesna NOT routinely needed at R-CHOP doses (750 mg/m²) but mandatory for high-dose conditioning (>1500 mg/m²).
Standard TLS prophylaxis when initiating: Standard TLS-profylax vid initiering av kemoterapi hos patienter med hög tumörbörda. Starta 24-48 timmar före behandling.
Standard VTE prophylaxis for lenalidomid: Standard VTE prophylaxis for lenalidomide-treated MM patients without additional VTE risk factors. For higher-risk patients (prior VTE, immobility, central venous catheter, active disease at induction) switch to LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily) or apixaban. Hold aspirin if platelets <50K.
